footer_timing: B200: zeroed timing inputs; 2,000 warmup; median of 5 × 301-launch CUDA-event batches; 32 MiB workspace.
footer_scope: *Exhaustive = stated finite config grid. Left: historical first-heuristic baseline; SM count unverified.
notes:
B200 rerun on 2026-10-01, Colossus lease 6u1g-0001. NVIDIA B200, 148 SMs, sm_100a; GPU UUID a4674550-4882-a08d-60b1-5efde3790e39; 183359 MiB; driver 615.71.09; CUDA toolkit 13.4.92 / runtime API 13040; cuBLASLt 130800 (13.8.0); rustc 1.100.0-nightly (e457a7b0d 2026-08-27). Power limit 1000W; clocks were not locked. Separate snapshots during the run showed SM clock 1830MHz / memory 4000MHz; these are not per-timing-window clock measurements. No other compute processes were observed in snapshots; runs sequential. Repository revision is recorded in source_revision; benchmark code changes were uncommitted, with source/binary SHA256 fingerprints and patch retained in the evidence bundle.

Workload: square M=N=K 4096,8192,16384, dense GEMM, alpha 1 beta 0, FP16 A/B with contiguous K and FP32 accumulation. Rust gemm_sol_final writes BF16 row-major; cuBLASLt uses FP16 column-major output (TN descriptors). Exact FP16-input/BF16-output probe returned CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED(status15). These remain closest-supported 2-byte-output comparisons, not identical output conversion/storage.

Final timing for all series: zero-filled inputs, 2000 warmup launches followed by five independent CUDA-event batches of 301 launches. Latency is median batch mean; TFLOP/s=2MNK / median seconds /1e12. No host copies, tuning, or validation included. Each shape is reported separately. Five raw batch samples are retained in the JSON. These throughputs should not be directly compared with slide 5: that comparison uses a different shape/kernel and nonzero timing inputs.

Top8: ask cuBLASLt for 8 heuristic candidates; screen valid results, refine all 8 with five 31-launch batches after 10 warmup launches per batch. Exhaustive-grid: dynamically enumerate all 26 returned algorithm IDs, capability tile/stage lists, all cluster enums, custom options, swizzles and supported reduction masks. Finite splitK values 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,8,12,16,32; 0/1 use no reduction. Inner MMA shape is library default, as in NVIDIA's custom-find sample. No 16-ID/100-result truncation. Check every configuration with AlgoCheck and a 32 MiB workspace limit; screen every supported fitting configuration with 1 warmup + 5 launches. Refine fastest 16 screening candidates plus all top 8 candidates with five 31-launch batches, then independently remeasure the selected winner using the final protocol above. 'Exhaustive' therefore means this stated finite configuration grid, not all possible integers or undocumented library implementations.

Correctness: both Rust variants passed full 16,777,216-output exact-BF16 Walsh-fingerprint validation at 4096 cubed. This does not establish full-output correctness at 8K/16K. Each final cuBLASLt winner passed 64 independent CPU dot-product checks at distributed coordinates on nonzero signed 1/8 inputs at its measured shape. Timing buffers then reset to zeros.

Reproduce from repository root:
bash crates/rustc-codegen-cuda/examples/gemm_sol_final/bench/build.sh
GEMM_SOL_MODE=both GEMM_CUBLAS_SKIP=1 GEMM_SOL_WARMUP=2000 GEMM_SOL_ITERS=301 GEMM_SOL_REPEATS=5 cargo oxide run gemm_sol_final --arch sm_100a
crates/rustc-codegen-cuda/examples/gemm_sol_final/bench/cublaslt_bench --mode both --warmup 2000 --iters 301 --repeats 5

Sources for tuning design:
https://github.com/NVIDIA/CUDALibrarySamples/blob/main/cuBLASLt/Common/LtMatmulCustomFind.h
https://github.com/NVIDIA/CUDALibrarySamples/blob/master/cuBLASLt/LtSgemmSimpleAutoTuning/sample_cublasLt_LtSgemmSimpleAutoTuning.cu

Only the B200 side is rerun. The smaller GPU results remain historical first-heuristic data; its SM count is unverified. Do not infer performance against tuned cuBLASLt on that unavailable GPU.
